text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 2440 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS

- Prime Minister Gyula Horn candidly admitted at his regular press conference that as a private individual he was shocked by the so-called Tocsik case, but as a prime minister he could do no other than to launch an investigation. @
- President Arpad Goncz was welcomed to Sweden yesterday at a reception by King Carl Gustav XVI.
- Prime Minister Gyula Horn is set to open a two-day visit to Germany today.
- Foreign Ministry spokesman Gabor Szentivanyi said that Hungarian diplomacy notes with regret that a decree has again been passed in Slovakia that is not in line with the basic treaty.
- Parliament Tuesday placed the ratification of the Hungarian-Romanian basic treaty on its agenda for urgent debate. @
- Only 4,000 people protested outside Parliament Tuesday to express their unhappiness with recent tuition fee increases.
- New MTV president Istvan Petak began work by sacking the head of the entertainment division because an "ordinary swindler" appeared on last Thursday's broadcast of a talk show.
- The State Debt Management Centre announced yesterday that Hungary will issue a total of 415 billion forints in bonds with maturity periods of 2-3 years in the last quarter of this year. @
NEPSZABADSAG

- Foreign Minister Laszlo Kovacs said he senses that Hungary is proceeding from the Partnership for Peace project to an alliance relationship when meeting US Chief National Security Adviser Anthony Lake and State Department Secretaries Strobe Talbott and Peter Tarnoff in the US.
- According to a proposed amendment to next year's VAT law already submitted to Parliament, VAT will no longer be refundable or tax deductible in cases of cash payment. @
- A poll shows Fidesz with 19 percent support among decided voters, placing them third behind the Socialists with 26 and the Smallholders with 22, and ahead of the Free Democrats at 14 percent.
- Next year, a total of 2,000 billion forints in state debt will be transferred to the State Debt Management Centre within the Ministry of Finance from the National Bank of Hungary.
- The Munich-based Siemens Matsushita Components Company has purchased Recotech Kft, based in Szombathely.
- The National Bank will introduce a new 100 forint coin into circulation from October 21. @
- Some 600 titles by four major English book publishers went on show at the National Szechenyi Library Tuesday and will also be up for sale.
MAGYAR NEMZET

- A poll conducted by the Hungarian Gallup Institute shows that 48 percent of those interviewed would support Hungary's admission to NATO if a referendum were to be staged on Sunday, while only 27 percent would answer with a definite no.
MAGYAR HIRLAP
- Hungary is expected to open an embassy in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia in the near future. @
NAPI GAZDASAG
- This paper carries a report on details of the 1997 budget submitted to Parliament on Monday.
VILAGGAZDASAG

- Magyar Hitel Bank has announced that a project to develop an extensive electronic retail banking service will go ahead with IBM. The new service, to be called Peoples' Bank, will be set up in the second quarter of 1997.
-- Budapest newsroom (36-1) 327 4040
